html:
Mulifanua, at the west end of Upolu, holds the only known Lapita site in Samoa, now under the sea. Pottery found there in 1973 dates the first settlers to roughly 800 BCE.

The settlers were people of the Lapita culture, who had sailed east from the islands near New Guinea and settled Fiji and Tonga shortly before. In Samoa and Tonga their descendants became the first Polynesians, over many centuries.

The pots were found by chance when a ferry wharf was dredged. Rising seas had covered the old shoreline, which is why so little of early Samoa has been found.
